rules.explanation: Embedded projects cannot be evaluated without knowing the underlying hardware topology, pin configurations, and component connections.
rules.do: Include clear circuit schematics (Proteus, KiCad, or Fritzing) and a explicit pin mapping table in the documentation.
rules.dont: Do not present embedded firmware without detailing the microcontrollers, sensors, and actuators connected.

rules.explanation: Writing monolithic embedded code inside main() limits portability and testability. Firmware should follow a layered architecture (MCAL, HAL, App layer).
rules.do: Separate hardware drivers, abstraction layers, and application logic into distinct modular C/C++ files.
rules.dont: Do not write entire embedded systems within a single main.c file or rely exclusively on high-level Arduino wrappers for professional engineering projects.

rules.rule_name: Resource Constraint and Memory Footprint Awareness
rules.explanation: Embedded microcontrollers have strict RAM/Flash limitations. Proper memory allocation and static allocation usage prevent stack overflows.
rules.do: Prefer static allocation over dynamic allocation (malloc/free) and document memory footprints (RAM/Flash usage).
rules.dont: Do not use unbounded recursion or unmonitored dynamic memory allocation in resource-constrained microcontrollers.

rules.explanation: Long-running operations inside an ISR block critical interrupts and break real-time deadlines.
rules.do: Keep ISRs short and deterministic by setting volatile flags or offloading work to main loops/OS tasks.
rules.dont: Do not execute blocking delay functions, heavy calculations, or serial prints inside interrupt routines.
